# Results — Phases 8–9: evaluation matrix, latency arm and hypothesis scoring (simulation only)

<!-- Generated by scripts/report.py from committed files under results/e08/ only; do not edit by hand. `make report` re-renders it byte-identically. -->

Simulation only: PyBullet physics, images rendered by PyBullet's TinyRenderer; model scale, λ = 1/25.
Every student here is distilled from a privileged, state-based P8 teacher and flies P8's frozen episode lists under P8's frozen success criteria (closing speed along the deck normal ≤ 0.5 m/s, lateral offset ≤ 0.10 m, relative tilt ≤ 15°, contact ≥ 0.5 s), all model scale.

Reading rules (P3-D1 §1, §6): learned cells are `IQM [stratified-bootstrap 95 % CI]` over seeds; baselines are `rate [Wilson 95 %] k/N`; contrasts are paired bootstraps over identical episodes; a difference exists only when its 95 % CI excludes 0; magnitudes are judged on the point estimate. No multiplicity correction is applied (P3-D1 §1). Sea states are never pooled. Every SS6 contrast carries P8's one-ulp flip floor: 6.6 % of `id` SS6 policy-episodes flip under at least one of 20 one-ulp draws (single-draw median 1.9 %), measured on P8's MLPs, not on these students.

Losses per 1 000 seed-episodes (learned) or per N (baselines): C crash, O off_pad, H hard_landing, B bounce, T timeout.

† outside the training distribution: no SS6 and no 90° heading in any training, tuning or selection (P3-D1 §2); `unseen_heading` is the 90° list. `unseen_vessel` and `static` are also not in the `train` pool (frigate SS3–SS5 only) and are not marked.

## 4. Secondary metrics (core arms)

Learned arms: the mean over seeds of each seed's cell value (sums for counts); baselines: the cell value. Touchdown metrics over contact-detected touchdowns only, never imputed. Speeds m/s, lengths m, times s, model scale; effort and jerk in P8's normalised action units; teacher agreement is the mean ‖a_student − a_teacher‖ on the student's own states.

## 5. Hypotheses (scored exactly as frozen in P3-D1 §6)

Verdict words are P3-D1's: supported / not supported / inconclusive. Nulls are reported here, in the body. No multiplicity correction is applied (P3-D1 §1).

### H1 — compounding error: `bc_dagger` − `bc_matched` — `id SS5`

- **Verdict: inconclusive** (CI excludes 0; estimate positive but below +5 points).
- Estimate: +2.6 points [+0.6, +4.8]; magnitude +5 points; in simulation.
- Contrast: success(bc_dagger) - success(bc_matched); statistic: P8 paired_bootstrap (seeds per arm, shared episodes; 10 000 reps, seed 20261023).
- N: 200 paired episodes; seeds `bc_dagger` 5, `bc_matched` 5.
- Inputs: `core bc_dagger id SS5`, `core bc_matched id SS5`.
- post hoc, not scored: paired_iqm_difference: +2.3 points [+0.3, +5.2] (1 decimal).
- reference arm success (mean over seeds x episodes): bc_matched 96.0 % (960/1000).
- labelled frames: bc_dagger: 616,053 (per seed 123,216, 123,013, 123,359, 123,223, 123,242); bc_matched: 614,365 (per seed 122,873, 122,873, 122,873, 122,873, 122,873).
- descriptive, not scored: success minus tunnelled successes: bc_dagger 986/1000 (tunnelled successes removed: 0); bc_matched 959/1000 (tunnelled successes removed: 1); difference +2.7 points (point estimate only, no CI; P8's tunnelled flag; the verdict uses success as P8 scores it).
- H1-SS6 beside it: +5.9 points [+2.3, +9.7] (1 decimal): supported.

Stated with the result (verbatim from the scorer):

- P8's paired_bootstrap treats seeds as unpaired, which is conservative here, because bc_dagger and bc_matched share iteration 0 (P3-D1 §6 H1).
- bc_dagger and bc_matched share iteration 0, the loop, the step count, the candidate set and the 2 000 starting conditions; they differ only in who chose the actions on the second 1 000 (P3-D1 §6 H1).
- Ceiling-limited: bc_matched is at 96.0 % (960/1000) in id SS5, so the largest attainable gain is 4.0 points, below +5; 'supported' was unattainable. The rule's verdict is kept (P3-D1 §6 ceilings; P8-D1 item 3).
- No multiplicity correction is applied (P3-D1 §1).

Stated with the result (verbatim from the scorer):

- Scored on 3 seeds per arm, the ablation count (P3-D1 §6 H2).
- The training mixture is 500 : 478 episodes after filtering, but about 1 : 2 by frames (gated episodes are longer) (P3-D1 §6 H2).
- All 22 filtered episodes are gated, mostly its longest waits (P3-D1 §6 H2).
- last_action in the proprio can reveal the mode after the first step (P3-D1 §6 H2).
- W1's bias grows as touchdowns get fewer, which works against an arm that times out (P3-D1 §6 H2).
- dp_mix's gain over dp is not shown to come from multimodality (Phase 8 before-you-start).
- select W1 (results/phase7/h2) is not H2 evidence (Phase 8 before-you-start).
- No multiplicity correction is applied (P3-D1 §1).

### H3 — chunk length: `dp` Ta = 1 − Ta = 8 (same checkpoints) — `id SS6`

- **Verdict: supported**.
- Estimate: +47.4 points [+41.0, +53.8]; magnitude +5 points; in simulation.
- Contrast: success(dp, Ta = 1) - success(dp, Ta = 8), same checkpoints, K = 10; statistic: joint-seed contrast (ila.eval.stats.joint_seed_contrast; 10 000 reps, seed 20261023).
- N: 200 paired episodes; seeds `dp` 5.
- Inputs: `dp_Ta dp id SS6 Ta1 K10 ens0`, `dp_Ta dp id SS6 Ta8 K10 ens0`.
- dp at Ta = 8 (mean over seeds x episodes): 33.8 %.
- SS6 flip floor: 6.6 % of `id` SS6 policy-episodes flip under at least one of 20 one-ulp draws (single-draw median 1.9 %), measured on P8's MLPs, not on these students.
- dp closed-loop flip rate (Phase 9): 32/150–44/150 episodes (21.3–29.3 %) change outcome class against the torch_cpu_fp32 reference under numeric perturbations of order 1e-5 (open-loop chunk max-abs <= 2.8e-05), the range over the flown scored fp32 providers (ort_cpu_fp32 33/150, ort_cuda_fp32 44/150, torch_cuda_fp32 32/150); measured on this dp's 150 select episodes in Phase 9 (closed-loop parity), not on a frozen list (seed 0's selected checkpoint; results/latency/closed_loop.csv, parity.csv).

Stated with the result (verbatim from the scorer):

- Checkpoints were selected at Ta = 8 (P3-D1 §6 H3).
- Ta = 1 without ensembling can switch modes between replans; so a null cannot separate 'chunking is harmless' from 'replanning causes mode switching' (P3-D1 §6 H3).
- dp_minus_last_action (P7-D3 item 7) is a competing explanation for dp recovering at Ta = 1: an input-freshness effect, stale last_action, alongside chunk length; any sentence that says dp fails 'because of chunking' must name it (P7-D3, Phase 8 before-you-start).
- P6-D5: a Ta contrast cannot attribute the loss to deck motion. On the frozen lists the gain is +53.3 / +53.2 / +47.4 points at SS4 / SS5 / SS6 (Ta = 1 minus Ta = 8, mean over seeds x episodes, same checkpoints; comparing the gains across sea states is an unpaired reading), and `dp` at Ta = 8 succeeds on 41.0 % (410/1000) of the static-deck episodes.
- No multiplicity correction is applied (P3-D1 §1).

### H4 — where the shortfall comes from: D = P − I — `id SS6`

- **Verdict: supported**.
- Estimate: +9.4 points [+5.6, +13.5]; magnitude D > 0; in simulation.
- Contrast: D = P - I; P = S(bc_state) - S(bc), I = S(teacher) - S(bc_state); statistic: three-arm bootstrap (ila.eval.stats.h4_three_arm_bootstrap; 10 000 reps, seed 20261023).
- N: 200 paired episodes; seeds `bc_state` 5, `bc` 5, `teacher ppo s0` 1.
- Inputs: `core bc_state id SS6`, `core bc id SS6`, `P8 committed ppo id SS6`.
- perception gap P: +9.5 points [+6.1, +13.3] (1 decimal).
- imitation gap I: +0.1 points [-1.1, +1.4] (1 decimal); ceiling-limited: I >= -1.5 points (teacher at 98.5 %).
- success (mean over seeds x episodes): teacher 98.5 %; bc_state 98.4 %; bc 88.9 %.
- SS6 flip floor: 6.6 % of `id` SS6 policy-episodes flip under at least one of 20 one-ulp draws (single-draw median 1.9 %), measured on P8's MLPs, not on these students.

Stated with the result (verbatim from the scorer):

- P includes the effect of withholding time_fraction, which bc_state sees and bc does not; P' = S(bc_state) - S(bc_plus_clock) is reported beside it, unscored (P3-D1 §6 H4).
- P' uses a bc_plus_clock that relies on the clock to a seed-dependent degree, and bc_state's clock reliance was not measured (Phase 8 before-you-start).
- P also includes bc_state's fp32 training against bc's bf16 (P3-D1 §3, §6 H4).
- H4 is conditional on teacher seed 0 (P8 ppo s0) (P3-D1 §1, §6 H4).
- I is ceiling-limited: the teacher is at 98.5 % at id SS6, so I = S(teacher) - S(bc_state) >= S(teacher) - 1 = -0.015; an imitation gap in bc_state's favour larger than that cannot be observed, which bounds how much of D can come from a negative I.
- No multiplicity correction is applied (P3-D1 §1).

### H5(a) — deployment latency (Phase 9) — `exported dp (K = 10), dp_e2e, batch 1`

- **Verdict: not supported** (no scored provider passed both parities and was timed). dp's closed-loop parity failure reflects outcome sensitivity of this dp, not a provider error: torch_cuda_fp32 runs the identical Python sampler as the torch_cpu_fp32 reference (torch eager, the DPStudent path) and still flips (32/150 > 3); open-loop chunk gaps are <= 2.8e-05 (results/latency/parity.csv); the flips go both ways (successes lost / gained: ort_cpu_fp32 12 / 16, ort_cuda_fp32 19 / 14, torch_cuda_fp32 14 / 12), and the provider success counts lie near the reference (ort_cpu_fp32 67, ort_cuda_fp32 58, torch_cuda_fp32 61 of 150 against 63, within ±5; results/latency/closed_loop.csv). The latency bound also fails independently on every timed scored provider: dp_e2e batch-1 p99 ort_cpu_fp32 122.911 ms, ort_cuda_fp32 52.6441 ms, torch_cuda_fp32 89.3851 ms (results/latency/h5a.csv), all > 33.3 ms, the model-scale 30 Hz control period (166.7 ms full scale); the measured wall-clock latency itself is on this machine (RTX A4000, WSL2) and is not scaled; not timed: ort_trt_fp16: refused (open-loop parity not passed). Phase 9 measured this dp's own closed-loop flip rate: 32/150–44/150 episodes (21.3–29.3 %) change outcome class against the torch_cpu_fp32 reference under numeric perturbations of order 1e-5 (open-loop chunk max-abs <= 2.8e-05), the range over the flown scored fp32 providers (ort_cpu_fp32 33/150, ort_cuda_fp32 44/150, torch_cuda_fp32 32/150); measured on this dp's 150 select episodes in Phase 9 (closed-loop parity), not on a frozen list (seed 0's selected checkpoint; results/latency/closed_loop.csv, parity.csv).
- Lowest p99 among scored providers passing open- and closed-loop parity: n/a; bound p99 < 33.3 ms, the model-scale 30 Hz control period (166.7 ms full scale; P3-D1 §6); the p99 is wall clock on this machine (RTX A4000, WSL2) and is not scaled.
- Contrast: p99(dp_e2e, batch 1) < 33.3 ms, the model-scale 30 Hz control period (166.7 ms full scale), on at least one scored provider that passes open- and closed-loop parity (P3-D1 §6 H5(a)); the p99 is wall clock on this machine and is not scaled; statistic: p99 of >= 2 000 timed batch-1 calls after >= 200 warm-up calls (P8's latency harness through ila.p8_adapter; P9-D1 item 8).

### H5(b) — latency in the loop (Phase 9) — `id SS5`

- **Verdict: not supported** (CI lower bound below -3 points).
- Estimate: -15.9 points [-21.5, -10.5]; magnitude non-inferiority margin: CI lower bound ≥ -3 points; in simulation.
- Contrast: success(dp, latency arm, d = 6) - success(dp, synchronous), same checkpoints, Ta = 8, K = 10, no ensembling; statistic: joint-seed contrast (ila.eval.stats.joint_seed_contrast; 10 000 reps, seed 20261023).
- N: 200 paired episodes; seeds `dp` 5.
- Inputs: `latency_arm dp id SS5 Ta8 K10 ens0`, `core dp id SS5 Ta8 K10 ens0`.
- delay: d = 6 control steps = 6 × 33.3 ms = 200.0 ms of model-scale sim time (6 × 166.7 ms = 1000.0 ms at full scale, as sim time); from results/latency/delay.json: provider torch_cpu_fp32, row dp_e2e, batch-1 p99 181.33390504546696 ms wall clock, fallback True; the measured wall-clock latency itself is on this machine (RTX A4000, WSL2) and is not scaled.
- why d: d = 6 is the torch_cpu_fp32 (1 thread) fallback delay from results/latency/delay.json (dp_e2e batch-1 p99 181.3 ms wall clock; ceil(181.3 / 33.333) = 6), because no scored provider passed open- and closed-loop parity (P3-D1 §7). Under §7's rule, the fastest open-loop-passing scored provider, ort_cuda_fp32 (dp_e2e batch-1 p99 52.6441 ms, results/latency/h5a.csv), would have given d = ceil(52.6441 / 33.333) = 2 (every open-loop-passing scored provider: ort_cuda_fp32 -> d = 2, torch_cuda_fp32 -> d = 3, ort_cpu_fp32 -> d = 4); those delays were not flown. The verdict is unchanged; the measured wall-clock latency itself is on this machine (RTX A4000, WSL2) and is not scaled.
- zero-action start: the contrast includes the d = 6 zero-action steps at the start of every episode (6 × 33.3 ms = 200.0 ms of model-scale sim time (6 × 166.7 ms = 1000.0 ms at full scale, as sim time); P3-D1 §7), which cannot be separated out of the estimate. The verdict is unchanged.
- success (mean over seeds x episodes): latency arm 20.2 % (202/1000); synchronous 36.1 % (361/1000).
- outcome classes, seed-episodes: latency arm: crash 23, off_pad 557, hard_landing 133, bounce 85, success 202, timeout 0 (of 1000); synchronous: crash 2, off_pad 462, hard_landing 103, bounce 72, success 361, timeout 0 (of 1000).
- dp closed-loop flip rate (Phase 9): 32/150–44/150 episodes (21.3–29.3 %) change outcome class against the torch_cpu_fp32 reference under numeric perturbations of order 1e-5 (open-loop chunk max-abs <= 2.8e-05), the range over the flown scored fp32 providers (ort_cpu_fp32 33/150, ort_cuda_fp32 44/150, torch_cuda_fp32 32/150); measured on this dp's 150 select episodes in Phase 9 (closed-loop parity), not on a frozen list (seed 0's selected checkpoint; results/latency/closed_loop.csv, parity.csv).

Stated with the result (verbatim from the scorer):

- No two-sided reading for H5(b): a CI wholly above 0 is non-inferior and reported as such (P3-D1 §6).
- Same checkpoints on both sides (the core dp selections); each replicate resamples seed indices jointly for both sides (P3-D1 §1). The parity verdicts behind d were measured on seed 0's selected checkpoint and apply to all five seeds (P3-D1 §3).
- The delay is simulated: PyBullet does not advance while the network computes; each request's result is computed when it is issued, on the CPU fp32 single-sample path, and held back d control steps (P3-D1 §7; P9-D1 item 10). Both sides fly that same path (P3-D1 §3).
- One request in flight at a time; the returned chunk executes from index (To - 1) + d, and past Tp - 1 its last action is held (from d > 7 at To = 2, Tp = 16, Ta = 8); the first action of an episode is zero until the first result lands (P3-D1 §7).
- d comes from a p99 measured on this machine (RTX A4000, i9-10980XE, WSL2); no embedded target is measured (P3-D1 §6 H5).
- last_action in proprio carries the applied (delayed) action, a feedback channel the student never saw in training; no teacher-under-delay reference exists to attribute the loss.
- Synchronous core dp at Ta = 8 succeeds on 36.1 % (361/1000) at id SS5; 33.8 % (338/1000) at id SS6; 41.0 % (410/1000) at static (mean over seeds x episodes). H5(b) compares this dp, distilled from P8 ppo s0, with itself, so a low baseline does not invalidate the contrast; non-inferiority is relative to that baseline (Phase 9 before-you-start).
- No multiplicity correction is applied (P3-D1 §1).

## 7. Tagged sections (never mixed into the core tables)

### 7a. `dp` chunk length Ta, with and without temporal ensembling (tag `dp_Ta`; `dp` distilled from P8 `ppo` seed 0; same checkpoints, K = 10; unscored curve)

Ta = 8 without ensembling is the core `dp` row (shared, not re-flown); Ta = 1 with ensembling is recorded as an alias of Ta = 1 without (one source of weight 1.0, same noise keys; P6-D1 item 3).

`dp` is reported at its frozen Ta = 8, K = 10 (P3-D1 §3); nothing is re-selected from this curve. Stated with it, from Phase 6 (`docs/protocol.md` P6-D5, items 3–5 and its README requirements; sources under `results/phase6/` and `results/dp_sweeps.json`): on `select`, `dp` at Ta = 8 already landed far below the BC family, mostly a chunking effect that did not depend on sea state; its checkpoint selection is noise-dominated and the selected `select` scores are optimistic; and held-out denoising loss is not a selection proxy (success does not follow it). H3 (§5) scores Ta = 1 − Ta = 8 at `id` SS6 with its caveats: checkpoints selected at Ta = 8, mode switching between replans, the `dp_minus_last_action` input-freshness confound, and P6-D5's: a Ta contrast cannot attribute the loss to deck motion.

It is below P8 ppo seed 0 (0.985) and above gated alone (0.630), unpaired reading; it is not above ppo s0, the better of its two teachers, and the training mixture was success-filtered. It lands harder than the reference: closing-speed p95 0.532 vs 0.282 m/s model scale, 14 tunnelled vs 0, 23 of 526 successes within 5 % of a success-criterion threshold vs 0 of 166. Not H2 evidence (H2 is scored at id SS4). SS6 is outside the training distribution; P8's one-ulp flip floor (6.6 % of id SS6 policy-episodes, measured on P8's MLPs, not on these students). In simulation.

### 7f. Latency in the loop (tag `latency_arm`; `id` SS4–SS6; P3-D1 §7)

Simulated delay of d control steps of sim time (33.3 ms model scale each, 166.7 ms at full scale), d from the batch-1 p99 wall clock measured on this machine (RTX A4000, WSL2; not scaled; `results/latency/delay.json`). PyBullet does not advance while a network computes: each request's result is computed when it is issued, on the CPU fp32 single-sample path, and held back d steps; one request is in flight at a time. Its numbers are withheld from every table above until `results-skeptic` has reviewed the touchdown audit (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 8).
